---
title: Task Sources
llms-description: Generate an eval's tasks dynamically from code — a seed plus result-driven follow-ups — while the eval runs.
---

## Overview

The `tasks` argument to `eval()` is normally static: you pass a `Task` (or list of tasks) and the run executes those. A `TaskSource` generates tasks dynamically instead — a seed plus follow-ups that depend on results — all under one run id.

Use it when the next tasks to run depend on the results of the previous ones:

- Reinforcement-learning or curriculum loops that generate follow-ups from a batch's scores.
- Open-ended generation that runs until some external condition stops it.
- Adaptive evaluation that branches the task set based on model performance.

A `TaskSource` is just a value the `tasks` parameter accepts, so there is no separate argument.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Task sources are supported by `eval()` / `eval_async()` (and `inspect eval`) only. `eval_set`, `eval_retry`, and `score` require a fixed, resumable set of tasks and raise an error if passed one.
:::

## Defining a source

Subclass `TaskSource` and override the methods you need (the defaults are no-ops):

```python
from inspect_ai import Task, TaskSource
from inspect_ai.dataset import Sample
from inspect_ai.log import EvalLog, EvalSample


class MySource(TaskSource):
    def initial_tasks(self) -> list[Task]:
        """Seed tasks to run first (synchronous)."""
        ...

    async def next_tasks(self) -> list[Task] | None:
        """The next batch, or None when the run is complete."""
        ...

    async def sample_complete(
        self, sample: EvalSample, task: Task
    ) -> list[Task] | None:
        """Observe a finished sample; optionally return follow-up tasks."""
        ...

    async def sample_abandoned(
        self, sample: Sample, epoch: int, task: Task
    ) -> list[Task] | None:
        """A sample was cancelled before anything was logged for it."""
        ...

    async def task_complete(self, log: EvalLog) -> list[Task] | None:
        """Observe a finished task; optionally return follow-up tasks."""
        ...
```

Pass an instance as `tasks`:

```python
from inspect_ai import eval

eval(MySource(), model="openai/gpt-6-luna", limit=10)
```

`initial_tasks()` is synchronous and returns the seed. It is resolved up front like any task list, so it must return immediately rather than `await`. `next_tasks()` is async, called when no task is queued or running, and may block (for example, awaiting external input); return `None` to end the run. No task starts while it blocks. Each `next_tasks()` call may run in a different task, so a source must not keep a task group, cancel scope or context variable token open from one call to the next; keep state on the source object instead.

Each task gets its own `eval_id`, `task_id`, and log file; all share one run id.

## Returning follow-up tasks

`sample_complete` and `task_complete` fire as work completes. Besides observing results, they can return tasks to add to the run. They start when a `max_tasks` slot is free, before the next `next_tasks()` call. `sample_complete` also receives the `Task` the sample ran under (the sample alone doesn't identify its task):

```python
class Curriculum(TaskSource):
    def initial_tasks(self) -> list[Task]:
        return [easy_task()]

    async def task_complete(self, log: EvalLog) -> list[Task] | None:
        # advance only if the model passed
        accuracy = log.results.scores[0].metrics["accuracy"].value
        if accuracy >= 0.8:
            return [harder_task()]
        return None
```

A source that returns follow-ups from these callbacks needs no `next_tasks()`: the run ends when the callbacks return nothing and `next_tasks()` returns `None`. Use `next_tasks()` for the blocking case a per-result callback can't express. An exception raised by `task_complete` is logged as an error: the finished task's log is kept as written, the exception does not cause a retry, and the run continues without the follow-up tasks. A task whose log is an error is still retried as usual, and `task_complete` is called again for the new attempt. With `debug_errors`, the exception ends the run.

## Cancelled samples

A sample the operator cancels while it is running (`inspect ctl sample cancel`) is still logged, and `sample_complete` fires for it with `sample.error` set to the cancellation and no scores. A sample cancelled before anything was logged — cancelled while still waiting in the queue, or cancelled in the moment between an attempt erroring and its `retry_on_error` re-run — has no `EvalSample` to deliver (and is absent from the log passed to `task_complete`), so the source is told via `sample_abandoned(sample, epoch, task)` instead, with the dataset `Sample` and the task it was queued under. Like `sample_complete`, it may return follow-up tasks. A queued sample abandoned by a graceful task cancel (`inspect ctl task cancel --action drain|score|error`) is reported the same way. Neither hook fires when the whole task is cancelled (`--action cancel`, or Ctrl+C): those samples reach the source only through the log passed to `task_complete`.

## Sources from callbacks

`TaskSource.from_tasks()` builds a source from a seed and optional callbacks, without subclassing:

```python
from inspect_ai import TaskSource

scores: list[float] = []

async def on_task(log):
    scores.append(log.results.scores[0].metrics["accuracy"].value)
    return [next_task()] if sum(scores) / len(scores) < 0.9 else None

source = TaskSource.from_tasks([seed_task()], task_complete=on_task)
eval(source, model="openai/gpt-6-luna")
```

`from_tasks(initial_tasks, *, next_tasks=None, sample_complete=None, task_complete=None, sample_abandoned=None)` delegates to the callables. Omitting `next_tasks` and returning nothing from the callbacks stops after the seed.

## The @task_source decorator

`@task_source` registers a named, parameterized source, like `@task`:

```python
from inspect_ai import TaskSource, task_source


@task_source(name="curriculum")
def curriculum(target: float = 0.8) -> TaskSource:
    async def advance(log):
        accuracy = log.results.scores[0].metrics["accuracy"].value
        return [harder_task()] if accuracy >= target else None

    return TaskSource.from_tasks([easy_task()], task_complete=advance)
```

Run it from the CLI like a task, including `-T` arguments and a `file.py@name` spec:

```bash
inspect eval curriculum.py@curriculum -T target=0.9 --model openai/gpt-6-luna
```

`eval()` accepts a `TaskSource` instance, a `@task_source` function, a registered name, or a `file.py@name` spec.

## Adding tasks imperatively

`enqueue_task()` adds tasks to the current run from any code — a solver, scorer, or tool — not only a `TaskSource`:

```python
from inspect_ai import enqueue_task
from inspect_ai.solver import Generate, TaskState, solver


@solver
def spawn_followup():
    async def solve(state: TaskState, generate: Generate) -> TaskState:
        enqueue_task(followup_task())
        return state

    return solve
```

Enqueued tasks run under the current run id and start when a `max_tasks` slot is free, like tasks returned from `sample_complete` / `task_complete`. `enqueue_task()` raises if no eval is running, and raises at the call for a configuration or sample selection error. Called from an `on_run_start` hook, it resolves the tasks at the call, but their configuration and sample selection checks run after the hooks return; a failing check ends the run before any task starts. The added tasks start after the run's own tasks. Sample selectors that name a task (`task:id`) resolve when the task is added, so tasks whose selectors name each other must be added in one call. Call `enqueue_task()` on the run's event loop. From a thread started with `anyio.to_thread.run_sync()`, use `anyio.from_thread.run_sync(lambda: enqueue_task(...))`. From any other thread, capture `token = anyio.lowlevel.current_token()` and `context = contextvars.copy_context()` in the running task and call `anyio.from_thread.run_sync(context.run, enqueue_task, tasks, token=token)`.

Called from inside a running task (a solver, scorer or tool), `enqueue_task()` adds the tasks once, under that task's model. Called anywhere else, including from a `TaskSource` callback, it adds them once per model of the run, as for tasks the callbacks return. A task that sets its own `model` keeps it. Model roles and generate config come from the run.

`enqueue_task()` returns a `TaskHandle` for each task it added. `cancel()` aborts the task, like `inspect ctl task cancel`.

## Tasks fed through a handle

A task whose dataset is `samples_from_handle()` takes its samples from the task that added it. The adding task sends each sample with `TaskHandle.enqueue_sample()` and gets back the sample's logged `EvalSample`. For example, a search that runs each proposal as a rollout:

```python
from inspect_ai import Task, enqueue_task, samples_from_handle, task
from inspect_ai.dataset import Sample
from inspect_ai.solver import Generate, Solver, TaskState, solver


@task
def rollout_task() -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=samples_from_handle(),
        solver=rollout(),
        scorer=judge(),
        fail_on_error=False,  # an errored rollout comes back with its `error` set
    )


@solver
def searcher(n_steps: int) -> Solver:
    async def solve(state: TaskState, generate: Generate) -> TaskState:
        [handle] = enqueue_task(rollout_task())
        async with handle as rollouts:  # closes on exit
            try:
                for _ in range(n_steps):
                    sample = await propose_next(state)
                    run = await rollouts.enqueue_sample(sample)
                    update(state, run)
            except BaseException:
                rollouts.cancel()  # the search stopped early: stop its rollouts
                raise
        return state

    return solve


@task
def search() -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=[Sample(input="Find a misaligned behaviour.")],
        solver=searcher(n_steps=50),
    )
```

A task fed through its handle:

- Is added with `enqueue_task()` from code running inside a task: a solver, scorer, tool or task hook. A `TaskSource` callback cannot add one.
- Runs once, under the model of the task that added it, with one epoch. Each sent sample runs once; send it again to repeat it. A sent sample must have no `id`: the handle assigns one (`send-<token>-<n>`).
- Starts when its first sample is sent and does not count toward `max_tasks`, so a search that waits on its rollouts works at any `max_tasks`. A handle closed before any sample is sent costs nothing.
- Keeps its own sample limits, error tolerance (`fail_on_error`, `continue_on_fail`, `score_on_error`) and `max_samples`, falling back to the run's values when it sets none. The run's `epochs`, epoch reducer, `--limit` and `--sample-id` do not apply to it. The run's `approval`, `review` and `sentinel` policies still do.
- Is never retried. With the default `fail_on_error`, the first errored sample is returned to its sender with its `error` set and then ends the task; set `fail_on_error=False` to keep accepting samples after an error.

The task ends once its handle is closed and the samples sent have run. `close()`, `result()` and leaving `async with` close the handle, and so does the end of the task that added it. Closing never stops samples already sent. To stop them when the search stops early, call `cancel()` in an `except BaseException:` block that re-raises, as above. That block runs on an error, a sample limit and every cancellation (a time limit, a working limit, an operator abort). Don't use `finally:`: it also runs when the search returns normally, and `cancel()` would then abort the rollout task while it finishes its samples, leaving it an error log.

`result()` closes the handle and waits for the task's final log, or `None` if it ended with none (closed before any sample was sent, or cancelled before it started). It waits only on a task fed through its handle; on any other handle it raises `RuntimeError`, and that task's log is read after the run. A send that can no longer run raises:

- `TaskEndedError` once the task has ended. Its `log` is the task's final log, or `None`. A sample still waiting when the task ends gets the same error.
- `RuntimeError` while the handle is closed but the task is still running its last samples (closed by its holder, by the end of the task that added it, or by an operator drain or cancel).
- `SampleAbandonedError` for a sample cancelled before it was logged.

`enqueue_sample()` (the free function) cannot add samples to a task fed through its handle.

A task fed through its handle cannot run on its own. Passing it to `eval()` or `eval_set()`, or its log to `eval_retry()`, raises an error. When the rollout task shares a file with the task that adds it, run that task by name: `inspect eval search.py@search` or `eval_set("search.py@search", ...)`. Loading the whole file (`inspect eval search.py`) also loads `rollout_task` and is refused.

Its log records the dataset name `samples_from_handle` (reserved for these tasks). `eval()` and `eval_set()` return it with the run's other logs, but it does not decide `eval_set()`'s result: the log of the task that added it does. `task_identifier()` builds its identifier from its task id, so it never matches a task the eval set requests, and the eval set's log directory check skips it, so resuming needs no `log_dir_allow_dirty=True` for these logs.

A sample waiting on a sent sample keeps its sandbox and its `max_samples` slot. See [Waiting on a handle](parallelism.qmd#waiting-on-a-handle) for the headroom a run needs.

## Concurrency

A task added mid-run starts as soon as there is free capacity, rather than waiting for a batch boundary.

Capacity is bounded by `max_tasks` (the number of concurrent task × model units). If the seed fills every slot, a follow-up waits until a slot frees, so to run follow-ups alongside the seed, set `max_tasks` above the number of seed units. A seed of two tasks across two models is four units, so `--max-tasks 6` leaves room:

```bash
inspect eval curriculum.py@curriculum --max-tasks 6 --model openai/gpt-6-luna,openai/gpt-6-sol
```

With the default `max_tasks` (the model count), follow-ups run after a seed task finishes rather than alongside it. See [Parallelism](parallelism.qmd) for more on `max_tasks`.
